description: Wall-mounted hook that cradles a ukulele by its neck, behind the headstock.

hardware.notes: Countersunk/pan head; length to suit wall type. Use wall anchors for drywall.

printing_notes: Orientation matters more than infill: lay the flat wall-facing back of the plate on the bed with the prongs pointing up. The exported STL stands the plate on its bottom edge, so re-orient it in the slicer (Bambu Studio's auto-orient picks this face).

Spend the print budget on walls, not infill. The bending load at the prong root is carried by the perimeters — set wall loops to 5-6 and top/bottom shells to 5, with 40% gyroid sparse infill. Jumping to 100% infill without raising the wall count costs a lot of time for much less strength.

In this orientation the prong roots are loaded across the layer lines, so tune for interlayer bonding: 0.15-0.16 mm layers, nozzle temperature near the top of the filament's range (about +10 C), and part-cooling fan reduced to roughly 30-50% on the walls.
PLA creeps under sustained load — an instrument left hanging for months will slowly bend the prongs. PETG, PLA+/Tough PLA, ASA or a PC blend are better choices for a permanent wall hook.

The upturned prong tips are horizontal cylinders in this orientation and their undersides may droop slightly. Supports (build-plate-only) give a cleaner tip; the droop is cosmetic and away from the load-bearing root.
Drive both wall screws and use anchors in drywall. A hook hanging on one screw can rotate and put the whole instrument's weight on a single prong.
